# JBM Packaging opens new site in Lebanon, Ohio

The building has 28ft clear-height ceilings and dense warehouse racking to improve movement of materials and completed goods.

 Vidhya Edwards Munnangi September 3, 2026 

The facility will support up to 50 additional jobs. Credit: Dawid G/ Shutterstock.com. 

JBM Packaging has opened a 52,500ft² site in Lebanon, Ohio, US, approximately a mile from its main base, as it expands its contract packaging, kitting and filling activities.

The facility will support up to 50 additional jobs.

It will house operations that had previously been run from rented premises in Queensgate, where JBM began its contract packaging business in 2021.

The new building has 28ft clear-height ceilings, dense warehouse racking and a layout intended to improve the movement of materials and completed goods.

JBM said the move lifts total machine capacity by 50%, giving it scope to handle a larger share of customers’ packaging requirements, including planning, production and distribution.

The facility allows the company to bring together several stages of work.

# Derse plans major expansion in Oak Creek

August 27, 2026

WEDC is supporting the project with $1.25 million in business tax credits

MADISON, WI. AUG. 27, 2026 – Derse, Inc., will build a new international headquarters in Oak Creek, a move that will prepare the company for long-term growth and create 65 new jobs.

Derse is a family-owned experiential marketing agency and exhibit builder for trade shows and events with locations in the United States and Europe. They design, build, and manage trade show exhibits, events, and environments for clients and have been recognized as an industry leader.

The $48 million project is the largest in the company’s nearly 80-year history and will consolidate two of the company’s eight existing locations into a 300,000-square-foot-facility on a 31-acre site with the Oakview Business Park in Oak Creek.

The Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation (WEDC) is supporting the project by authorizing up to $1.25 million in performance-based state income tax credits. The actual amount of the tax credits is contingent upon the number of jobs created and the amount of capital investment during the period

# RGL Logistics unveils new warehouse in Appleton

Added capacity needed to support region’s manufacturers, company says

RGL prioritizes career development, Michelle Wellens said, while also offering paid opportunities for community volunteer work. Submitted Photo

 

Judith Munson

Contributor

October 5, 2026

APPLETON – RGL Logistics is making moves again.

The Green Bay-based company recently completed construction on a new warehouse at its Appleton campus, marking its 29th building to join its three-campus network. 

Michelle Wellens, director of transportation solutions and marketing, said the new building adds 427,500 square feet to the company’s total footprint of more than 4 million square feet, which covers all three RGL sites in Neenah, Green Bay and Appleton.

Wellens said the warehouse was built to create additional capacity and flexibility on RGL’s Appleton campus, while continuing to respond to customers’ needs.
